fit_paragraphs.text: Prof. Fazeli's MMint Lab sits directly at the intersection of my three research threads. ViTaSCOPE fuses vision and tactile sensing for in-hand pose and extrinsic contact estimation [paper:W4414050430], which mirrors my undergraduate work building a 64-taxel piezoresistive fabric skin for slip detection [lib:cv]. The 'This&That' video-generation planner [paper:W4413917052] complements my IISc diffusion-policy pipeline, where 40 demonstrations on a $1,800 arm reached 78% on cup stacking [lib:cv]. The lab's stated focus on assistive care [advisor:Nima Fazeli] also aligns with my goal of deploying manipulation skills in elderly-care households [lib:interests].

Prof. Berenson's ARM Lab addresses the generalization problem I care most about. His work on learning generalizable trajectory sampling distributions for model predictive control [paper:W4392207744] maps directly onto my interest in policies that transfer across object instances and lighting conditions [lib:interests]. Constrained Stein Variational Trajectory Optimization [paper:W4400644189] provides a principled path toward the safety constraints I consider essential for household robots [lib:interests]. The lab's active focus on deformable object manipulation [advisor:Dmitry Berenson] connects to my towel-folding results (61% success, versus 29% for a behaviour-cloning baseline) [lib:cv].

Prof. Goyal's work on learning precise manipulation from few demonstrations using multi-view 3D representations [paper:W4402354093] speaks directly to my constraint of 40 demonstrations per task on low-cost hardware [lib:cv]. RVT-2's approach to spatial reasoning [paper:W4402354093] and the 3D-MVP pretraining strategy for cross-instance generalization [paper:W4413144893] would give my diffusion-policy pipeline a stronger perceptual backbone. My sim-to-real reconstruction work—cutting the success drop from 41 to 17 points using 12 phone photos [lib:cv]—could benefit from the 3D spatial pretraining direction Prof. Goyal's group pursues [advisor:Ankit Goyal].

Prof. Bucher's VLFM work demonstrates zero-shot semantic navigation by grounding vision-language models to frontier maps without task-specific retraining [paper:W4401417061], and the zero-shot object-centric instruction-following paper extends this to unstructured settings [paper:W4404390404]. Both directly address the domain-generalization challenge I encountered when transferring kitchen-counter policies across scenes [lib:cv]. Her lab's emphasis on sim-to-real and zero-shot transfer [advisor:Bernadette Bucher] would complement my real-to-sim reconstruction pipeline and my goal of deploying manipulation in diverse home environments [lib:interests].

sop.text:
The robot I want to build does not live in a lab: it handles a crumpled dish towel on a counter it has never seen, on hardware a family can afford. Three projects have shaped how I think about making that possible.

At IISc I built a diffusion-policy pipeline for a $1,800 six-degree-of-freedom arm [lib:cv]. With 40 teleoperated demonstrations per task the policy reached 78% success on cup stacking and 61% on towel folding, compared with 44% and 29% for a behaviour-cloning baseline [lib:cv]. The towel result is the one I return to: deformable objects expose the limits of vision-only sensing, which is why my undergraduate project at BITS Pilani constructed a 64-taxel piezoresistive fabric tactile skin that detected slip within 60 ms in 91% of trials [lib:cv]. Combining that kind of low-cost tactile feedback with visuomotor learning is the technical core of what I want to pursue.

The third thread is sim-to-real transfer. At TCS Research I reconstructed a kitchen counter from twelve phone photos and trained policies in the resulting scene; the success drop relative to the real counter was 17 percentage points rather than 41 points for a generic simulated scene [lib:cv]. That gap still matters, and closing it through domain randomisation and better scene reconstruction is a central goal for my PhD [lib:interests].

At Michigan I want to work with Prof. Nima Fazeli, whose MMint Lab combines visuo-tactile sensing and diffusion-based behavior cloning for contact-rich tasks [advisor:Nima Fazeli]. ViTaSCOPE's fusion of vision and touch for in-hand pose estimation [paper:W4414050430] is the closest published work to what I am trying to do with fabric tactile skins. I am also drawn to Prof. Dmitry Berenson's ARM Lab: the work on learning generalizable trajectory distributions [paper:W4392207744] addresses exactly the cross-instance generalization problem I hit with towel folding, and the Constrained Stein Variational Trajectory Optimization framework [paper:W4400644189] offers a rigorous path toward the safety constraints that household deployment requires [lib:interests].

Longer term, I want to deploy these systems in assistive-care settings for elderly users in Indian households [lib:interests]—an application domain that demands cheap hardware, robustness to clutter, and safe contact. Michigan's Robotics program, with its depth in manipulation and learning, is the right place to pursue that goal [lib:profile].

Arjun Mehta
